claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.8, annual return 9%, maximum drawdown 3%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.83 to 2.74 (change -0.08).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.83 to 0.26. Changed by strict mode: operators zscore_full, winsor_full.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 2.83 (as submitted, 10 bps: 2.83); it breaks even at above 200 bps with daily turnover 0.02.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.83 against 2.83 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 1.33 against 2.83 in research, a gap of +1.49.
The best year gives 18% of total P&L (year 1) and calm regimes give 65%; Sharpe is 2.39 in calm and 4.95 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 3 distinct specs; the best of 3 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.47, so the claimed 2.80 becomes 2.33 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.97 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.02, 95th percentile 0.64).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.83 to as low as 1.22 (as low as 1.67 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (20 days) give 23% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 13% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (pit_replay EX-2, holdout_test EX-5).
